remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
Not sure if anything in tech has ever gotten as much broad-based support and alignment as this post and message.

The key now is that America should actually step up and continue to push open weights innovation. It’s good for the entire market, including the frontier labs. 

Open weights accelerates the diffusion of AI across the economy by providing more options for specific customer requirements, can lower the cost of certain workloads, and you can tune models for areas of work that don’t always make sense in a horizontal frontier model.
remarks.translation: 不确定科技领域是否曾有哪篇文章或信息获得过如此广泛的支持与共识。关键在于，美国现在应当真正行动起来，持续推动开放权重创新。这对整个市场都有利，包括前沿实验室。开放权重通过为特定客户需求提供更多选择，加速了人工智能在经济领域的普及；它能降低某些工作负载的成本，还能针对那些在横向前沿模型中未必适用的工作领域进行模型调优。
remarks.observation: 这条言论适合观察模型运行、算力、存储、sandbox 或开发平台基础设施的变化；后续事实判断需回到原始公告或技术文档。

remarks.name: Boris Cherny
remarks.role: Claude Code anthropicai
remarks.text:
Opus 5 is a great model for coding, data analysis, design, biology, knowledge work.

More than any of these eval scores, what is most exciting to me is something else: Opus 5 is our least prompt injectable model yet. It is a bit buried in the system card, but across PI evals and red teaming, Opus 5 is very hard to prompt inject successfully.

And when layering defenses -- strong model alignment, combined with prompt injection probes, combined with Auto Mode in Claude Code -- the success rate for prompt injection attacks drops to ~0. This is new and exciting! More about this soon.

https://t.co/Tc7z2FqJhQ
remarks.translation: Opus 5 在编程、数据分析、设计、生物学和知识工作方面是一款出色的模型。比起这些评估分数，更让我兴奋的是另一件事：Opus 5 是我们迄今为止最不易被提示注入的模型。这在系统卡中有些被埋没，但根据 PI 评估和红队测试，Opus 5 很难被成功提示注入。而且当叠加防御措施——强大的模型对齐，结合提示注入探测，再结合 Claude Code 中的自动模式——提示注入攻击的成功率降至约 0。这是全新且令人振奋的进展！更多内容即将揭晓。 https://t.co/Tc7z2FqJhQ

remarks.name: Madhu Guru
remarks.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
remarks.text:
There is a massive opportunity over the next few years for people who know how to take messy real-world workflows and adapt foundation models to them.

Doing that requires understanding how work gets done, designing evals, improving models through post-training, and building the feedback loops that continuously improve models.

That’s how a general-purpose model becomes exceptional for a specific domain.

Today, that skillset is still concentrated in a handful of labs.
remarks.translation: 未来几年，对于懂得如何将混乱的现实工作流程适配基础模型的人来说，将存在巨大机遇。这需要理解工作如何完成、设计评估、通过后训练改进模型，并构建持续优化模型的反馈循环。这正是通用模型在特定领域变得卓越的途径。目前，这类技能仍集中在少数实验室手中。

remarks.name: Dan Shipper
remarks.role: ceo every
remarks.text:
BREAKING: Claude Opus 5 is OUT NOW!

And…it’s a hard model to love.

We’ve spent the last week @every testing it across coding, writing, knowledge work, and our internal agent.

It argued with instructions, stopped before the work was finished, and generally didn’t play well with our existing skills and plugins like Compound Engineering. Our first reaction was: What have they done to my boy?

Then we deleted our existing skills and started from scratch.

Without the elaborate workflows we had built for earlier models, Opus 5 got dramatically better, and even showed flashes of brilliance.

Here’s our Day 0 vibe check:

- It’s a poor man’s Fable. It has many of Fable’s personality quirks without Fable’s genius.
- It breaks backward compatibility. If you’re using it with existing skills and workflows, watch out. It will often stop early or otherwise miss your instructions.
- If you start from scratch, you’ll have better results. @KieranKlaassen figured out that if he just started from scratch without his existing skills, he could get dramatically better results. This is a model that takes some time to rebuild your workflows around—but if you do, there’s a payoff waiting.
- Medium or low effort works better. @KieranKlassenn also found better results using Opus 5 on lower thinking levels. It seems that the more time you give it to think, the more likely it is to do the more annoying behaviors. Don’t just switch to Sonnet for a faster response! Try low thinking.

I have two slots in my workflow:

1. The genius model I use for my biggest hardest tasks, currently Fable.
2. The smart, fast generalist I use for everything else, currently GPT-5.6.

Opus 5 has the personality of the genius, but doesn’t have its top end. So that puts it in a strange middle ground that doesn’t really have a home in my day to day. I think I’ll use it mostly when I run out of Fable tokens.

full vibe check on @every in the next tweet 👇
remarks.translation:
快讯：Claude Opus 5 现已发布！然而……这是一款让人爱不起来的模型。过去一周，我们在 @every 上对它进行了全面测试，涵盖编程、写作、知识型任务以及我们的内部智能体。它会跟指令对着干，活儿没干完就停手，而且跟我们现有的技能和插件（比如 Compound Engineering）配合得相当不顺畅。我们的第一反应是：他们把我的好搭档怎么了？于是我们删掉了现有技能，从零开始。没有了为早期模型构建的那些复杂工作流，Opus 5 的表现显著提升，甚至闪现出一些亮眼之处。以下是我们第 0 天的初步感受：

- 它像是低配版的 Fable。它有很多 Fable 的个性怪癖，却没有 Fable 的天才之处。
- 它破坏了向后兼容性。如果你把它用在现有技能和工作流上，千万要小心。它经常会提前终止，或者以其他方式忽略你的指令。
- 如果从零开始，你会得到更好的结果。@KieranKlaassen 发现，只要抛开现有技能从零开始，就能获得显著改善的效果。这是一款需要花些时间围绕它重建工作流的模型——但如果你这么做了，回报就在前方等着你。
- 中等或低投入效果更好。@KieranKlassenn 还发现，在较低思考级别上使用 Opus 5 效果更佳。似乎你给它思考的时间越长，它就越容易表现出那些令人恼火的行为。别为了更快响应就切换到 Sonnet！试试低思考模式。

我的工作流中有两个位置：
1. 用于最艰巨任务的天才模型，目前是 Fable。
2. 用于其他所有事务的聪明、快速的通用模型，目前是 GPT-5.6。

Opus 5 有着天才模型的个性，却没有它的顶尖能力。所以它处在一个奇怪的中间地带，在我的日常工作中找不到合适的位置。我想我主要会在 Fable 的 token 用完后才用它。

完整初步感受请见 @every 的下一条推文 👇

remarks.name: Aaron Levie
remarks.role: ceo box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
remarks.text:
Very happy to have Box sign this letter. We’re big believers in the power of open weights AI.

Open weights models help to drive the industry forward in a variety of ways to ensure more innovation, creativity, and diffusion of AI.

You get to have layers of the stack that emerge to post train models for highly specific purposes, which makes AI more useful in real world scenarios. Instead of waiting for just a few players to go deep in a domain, you get dozens or hundreds of attempts at that vertical, like in finance, life sciences, legal, healthcare, and more.

You get to see variance in how to handle safety and cyber risks. Instead of just one approach, you get a peek into what happens advanced capabilities can be used to build better systems to are used to defend systems. 

You get alternative approaches to training and building AI models. In more compute constrained environments, you develop more novel and efficient approaches to model training, which every other lab can learn from. 

And you get different cost structures for different workloads. High end and orchestration tasks can go to the closed frontier models and specific workhorse tasks can be done more cheaply. 

Open vs. closed is not a zero sum battle. The reason why you want strong open weights models is because it pushes the entire AI industry forward.
remarks.translation: 非常高兴Box能签署这封信。我们坚信开放权重AI的力量。开放权重模型以多种方式推动行业前行，确保更多创新、创造力与AI的广泛渗透。你可以获得堆栈中涌现的层级，针对高度特定的目的对模型进行后训练，这让AI在现实场景中更加实用。无需等待少数玩家深入某个领域，你就能看到数十甚至数百次针对该垂直领域的尝试，比如金融、生命科学、法律、医疗保健等等。你能观察到处理安全与网络风险的不同方式。不止一种方法，你可以一窥先进能力如何被用于构建更优系统，进而用于防御系统。你会获得训练和构建AI模型的替代方案。在计算资源更受限的环境中，你会开发出更新颖高效的模型训练方法，其他所有实验室都能从中学习。而且，不同工作负载会对应不同的成本结构。高端与编排任务可以交给封闭的前沿模型，而特定的主力任务则可以更经济地完成。开放与封闭并非零和博弈。之所以需要强大的开放权重模型，是因为它能推动整个AI行业向前发展。

remarks.text: Claude Code uses Bun written in Rust now
remarks.content: In Rewriting Bun in Rust Jarred Sumner made the following claim: Claude Code v2.1.181 (released June 17th) and later use the Rust port of Bun. Startup got 10% faster on Linux but otherwise, barely anyone noticed. Boring is good.</

podcasts.originalTitle: Factory's Matan Grinberg: The Coming ‘Dark Factory’ Where Software Builds Itself
podcasts.excerpt: 工厂于2023年4月开始打造全自主编程智能体，比企业真正准备好早了整整两年。马坦·格林伯格如今坦言，这无异于判断失误。这位Factory联合创始人兼CEO讲述了公司如何熬过那段"沙漠跋涉期"，包括在产品未能让开发者痴迷时，毅然将几乎全部收入返还给客户。马坦提出了一个反常规的技术观点：模型无关的集成框架，优于OpenAI和Anthropic等实验室偏好的模型与框架协同设计，因为让集成框架接触多种模型，能避免其过度适配任何单一模型。他认为，像GLM这样的开放权重模型，只需保持比前沿技术落后一代，就能以极低的成本占据大部分token使用量；而CIO们很快会像评估人力投入一样，为每个新增token的使用找到合理依据。展望未来，他预测90%的编程工作将……
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Factory started building fully autonomous coding agents in April 2023, two years before enterprises were ready. Matan Grinberg now says this is indistinguishable from being wrong. The Factory co-founder and CEO explains how the company survived its "journey in the desert," including the decision to hand nearly all of its revenue back to customers when the product wasn't making developers obsessed. Matan makes the contrarian technical case that a model-agnostic harness beats the model-and-harness co-design that labs like OpenAI and Anthropic favor, because exposing a harness to many models keeps it from overfitting to any single one. He argues open-weight models like GLM will capture the majority of tokens by staying one generation behind the frontier at a fraction of the cost, and that CIOs will soon justify every incremental token the way they justify headcount. podcasts.title: 第90集：人工智能先驱尤尔根·施密德胡伯谈当今AI现状
podcasts.originalTitle: Ep 90: AI Pioneer Jürgen Schmidhuber on the State of AI Today
podcasts.excerpt: 尤尔根·施密德胡伯博士，这位享誉全球的科学家与人工智能研究者，被公认为该领域的先驱之一。他通过其实验室的工作，孕育了当今Transformer架构、长短期记忆网络（LSTM）以及递归自我改进等关键理念。他认为，真正的通用人工智能（AGI）仍受限于物理硬件瓶颈；随着开源技术紧追封闭实验室的步伐，当前对AI数据中心的投资热潮即将迎来修正；而通往通用智能的路径，在于人工好奇心与自主生成的实验，而非依赖互联网数据。在结尾部分，他重新审视了主流AI安全论点，并描绘了一幅宏大愿景：自我复制的机器人社会终将殖民整个太阳系。 (0:00) 引言 (1:24) 超人类AI还有多远？ (2:27) ChatGPT为何未令他惊讶 (3:21) 递归自我改进之路 (9:01) AI会迎来爆发式飞跃吗…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: Dr. Jürgen Schmidhuber, a renowned scientist and AI researcher widely regarded as one of the pioneers in the field, originated key ideas behind today's transformers, LSTMs, and recursive self-improvement through his lab's work. He argues that true AGI remains bottlenecked by physical hardware, that today's AI data center investments are headed for a correction as open-source keeps pace with closed labs, and that the path to general intelligence runs through artificial curiosity and self-generated experimentation rather than internet data. He closes by reconsidering mainstream AI safety arguments and offers a sweeping vision of self-replicating robot societies eventually colonizing the solar system. podcasts.title: 与DoorDash联合创始人Andy Fang和Stanley Tang共同打造自主配送体验
podcasts.originalTitle: Building an Autonomous Delivery Experience with DoorDash Co-Founders Andy Fang and Stanley Tang
podcasts.excerpt: DoorDash 不仅仅是一家配送公司。从创立之初，联合创始人 Andy Fang 和 Stanley Tang 就将其作为一家机器人与自动驾驶公司来运营。Andy 和 Stanley 与 Sarah Guo 一起探讨了自动驾驶技术和人工智能如何重塑消费习惯、商业和配送。他们谈到了 Ask DoorDash 的推出，这是一个自然语言界面，既能推动餐厅发现，也能促进更大额的杂货订单。他们还讨论了 Dot，这是他们自主研发的自动驾驶配送机器人，已在凤凰城运营超过两年，并展示了他们在自动驾驶技术中面临并解决的运营和硬件挑战。Andy 和 Stanley 还谈到了自动驾驶配送中的“首尾 100 英尺问题”，为什么多模式策略是成功的关键，如何扩展自动驾驶和运营规模，以及为什么他们相信未来 DoorDash 需要更多而非更少的 Dasher。立即注册…
podcasts.originalExcerpt: DoorDash is not just a delivery company. From its inception, co-founders Andy Fang and Stanley Tang operated it as a robotics and autonomy company. Andy and Stanley join Sarah Guo to explain how autonomous tech and AI are reshaping consumer habits, commerce, and delivery. Andy and Stanley talk about the rollout of Ask DoorDash, a natural-language interface that’s driving both restaurant discovery and larger grocery orders. They also discuss Dot, their in-house autonomous delivery robot that has operated in Phoenix for over two years, and how it highlights the operational and hardware challenges they have faced and solved in autonomous tech.
